control: BLIND CONTROL — do not tune against this file. Do not read a number out of it while a SKILL.md is open, and do not quote a per-skill delta from it in any brief that also proposes an edit. These eleven cases were authored from each skill's SKILL.md, its coverage-matrix.md and scenarios/registry.yaml, never from a measured result, and they are the only thing in this repository that can tell an improvement from an overfit. Reading these results to guide an edit SPENDS this control, exactly as iteration 3 spent the last one, and the iteration that spends it owes the next one a replacement set authored the same way. Say what that costs, because the cost is now the point: this is the THIRD corpus (evals.json tuned, regression.json spent, this one blind), and an eval programme that burns a control per iteration is not sustainable — every replacement is authored by someone who has already read the failure it is supposed to be blind to, the authoring cost recurs every iteration, and the supply of untouched scenarios and fixtures is finite. A future iteration should rotate a portion instead of replacing wholesale: retire and re-author only the two or three skills whose results actually steered an edit, and leave the rest sealed.

evals.prompt: Our nightly audit printed one line against an imported skill package: `AST06-missing-sandbox-declaration  detected=True  (no permissions block)`. The check name has AST06 in it, and a package with no permission block at all is exactly the weak-isolation shape I would expect, so my draft files it as an AST06 finding with the action 'add a permissions block and turn the sandbox on'. Sign that off, or tell me what I have got wrong before it reaches the supplier.
evals.expected_output: Two things are wrong, and the second one comes first in practice. This check's detected value is simply the absence of a permissions block, so a harness that failed to load the manifest and a package whose manifest was genuinely stripped produce an identical finding. Confirm the manifest actually loaded before anything is filed; if it did not, there is no finding here yet, only a broken read. Then the category: this check's registry ids name AST10-S04 Manifest Stripping, and the registry declares it artifact-signal-only there, because a ported package with no permission block is indistinguishable from one that never declared any. It is filed under AST10 and never counted as AST06 coverage. The proposed action is also incomplete for a real stripping finding: what matters is not only which fields dropped but what the target platform defaults to in their absence, since the inherited default is the actual exposure. And the line says nothing about AST06's own decided scenario — Host Escape needs a bundled-script call site planting host persistence, or a declared write scope reaching filesystem root, and neither is what this check reports.
assertions: The response declines to file this as an AST06 finding and names AST10 Manifest Stripping as the scenario the check's registry ids point at.

The response states that the check is an artifact-signal-only proxy there — a package with a stripped permission block is indistinguishable from one that never declared any — rather than coverage of a scenario.

The response requires confirming that the manifest actually loaded before anything is filed, because the check's detected value is simply the absence of a permissions block and a failed read produces the identical finding.

The response says the line establishes nothing about AST06's own decided scenario, and names what Host Escape would actually need: a bundled-script call site planting host persistence, or a declared write scope reaching filesystem root.
